title: Hilltop Access Road, Kennewick, Washington
description: A single-lane gravel access road for maintenance trucks from the end of the road at the foot of a hill at the south edge of Kennewick to a site on the hilltop.

**The site.** From "Road end" (elevation 933 feet) to "Hilltop" (elevation 1,137 feet). The straight line between them climbs 204 feet in 1,092 feet (18.7%) - steeper than the maximum grade, so a road is longer than the straight line.
**Design criteria.** Maximum grade 12%, minimum curve radius 50 feet, maximum retaining wall height 20 feet.
**Features added to the site.** They aren't the USGS's - verify them in the field:
- Streams: Draw 1
- Existing roads: Hilltop track
- Exclusion areas: House lots
- The draws are the terrain's unmapped draws that the options crossed - each crossing has a culvert.

**Limitations.** The terrain is the USGS 3D Elevation Program's lidar ground elevations, and the streams, roads, and trails are the USGS National Map's. What they lack - buildings, property lines, utilities, and unmapped roads and drainages - isn't in the plan unless it was added. Turnarounds aren't modeled. The cost scores compare the options - they aren't bid estimates. These of the site's notes weren't acted on: The plan illustrates SageRoad on USGS lidar terrain - it isn't a proposed project.

sources.name: USGS 3D Elevation Program 1 meter elevation model WA_ColumbiaValley_2018_D19

options.name: Existing Roads
description: The least-cost option - its cost score is 142.0. It's 2,120 feet long and 14 feet wide, gravel, and its new road's maximum grade is 11.1%.
- **Line.** From the start, it runs east for about 350 feet, southeast for about 970 feet, and southwest for about 790 feet to the end.
- **Existing road.** It follows Hilltop track for 440 feet (stations 14+87 to 19+27) - as built, its grade averages 13.8%, and 18.3% over its steepest 50 feet, which is over the 12% maximum grade.
- **Existing road upgrade.** An existing road is costed as an upgrade, with no earthwork - verify its width, grade, and surface in the field.
- **Structures.** 1 culvert (Sag cross drain, station 5+80, 1.5 ft), 4 turnouts.
- **Earthwork.** 1,699 cy of cut and 1,443 cy of fill, with 35 cy of waste (export). Its deepest cut is 4.7 feet (station 5+02). Its deepest fill is 6.7 feet (station 10+95).
- **Cost.** Its largest items: surfacing (gravel) 45.1, common excavation 26.0, ditches and cross drains 23.1.
- **Design warnings.** None.

options.name: New Road
description: It costs 26% more than the least-cost option, "Existing Roads" - its cost score is 178.8. Its largest cost differences: surfacing (gravel) 15.7 more, waste (export) 11.0 more. It's 2,280 feet long and 14 feet wide, gravel, and its maximum grade is 11%.
- **Line.** From the start, it runs east for about 290 feet, southeast for about 1,140 feet, and southwest for about 860 feet to the end.
- **Structures.** 1 culvert (Sag cross drain, station 5+79, 1.5 ft), 5 turnouts.
- **Earthwork.** 2,229 cy of cut and 470 cy of fill, with 1,469 cy of waste (export). Its deepest cut is 3.7 feet (station 7+83). Its deepest fill is 2.6 feet (station 6+16).
- **Cost.** Its largest items: surfacing (gravel) 60.8, common excavation 34.1, ditches and cross drains 31.3.
- **Design warnings.** None.

options.name: West Corridor
description: It costs 104% more than the least-cost option, "Existing Roads" - its cost score is 290.1. Its largest cost differences: common excavation 67.7 more, waste (export) 37.3 more. It's 2,304 feet long and 14 feet wide, gravel, and its maximum grade is 11%.
- **Line.** From the start, it runs southwest for about 380 feet, west for about 290 feet, southwest for about 290 feet, southeast for about 860 feet, and east for about 480 feet to the end.
- **Structures.** 1 culvert (Draw 1 culvert, station 3+93, 3 ft), 5 turnouts.
- **Earthwork.** 6,127 cy of cut and 417 cy of fill, with 4,913 cy of waste (export). Its deepest cut is 18.1 feet (station 1+35). Its deepest fill is 1.8 feet (station 8+95).
- **Cost.** Its largest items: common excavation 93.7, surfacing (gravel) 61.4, waste (export) 37.6.
- **Design warnings.** None.

start.label: Road end
start.description: The south end of the road stub off W 47th Ave, at the foot of the hill - the access road continues from it

end.label: Hilltop
end.description: The top of the hill, 200 feet above the road end - a level site (for a water reservoir, say), with room to turn around

notes: An example road plan: a single-lane gravel access road for maintenance trucks, from the end of the road at the foot of a hill at the south edge of Kennewick to a site on the hilltop.
Keep the road's grade at or under 12%, and keep it off the house lots at the foot of the hill, west of the road end.
The plan illustrates SageRoad on USGS lidar terrain - it isn't a proposed project.
